correctness.rationale: The Fourier image of c_j f(a_j x+b_j) is (c_j/a_j)e^{ib_jη/a_j} f̂(η/a_j), supported within the target bandwidth. Real offsets leave the individual norm |c_j|/√a_j unchanged. Log frequencies give a shifted argument and coefficient d_j e^{ib_j e^x/a_j}. Independently, on the common intersection of the shifted length-R packet supports, of length R−(max ℓ_j−min ℓ_j), the offset-free output is e^{itx}m(t)/√R. For fixed R and t the offset error in norm tends to zero as the support moves to −∞ (uniform phase convergence and the individual norm bounds); unit packets there are weakly null, so any compact perturbation vanishes in norm on them. Sending R to infinity gives the required essential-norm lower bound for each t and all fixed real offset vectors. The full-line convolution upper bound at zero offsets holds on both frequency signs, so the exact unshifted norm is sup|m|. Maximizing over the compact relative-phase orbit closure gives L iff all summands align there; its annihilator is exactly the integer relations of the log ratios. This also verifies genericity and the squeeze for every approximation number. In the 1,2,4 example |m|²=11/4+x/√2−2x², x=cos θ, attaining 45/16 at x=1/(4√2). No attainment at a finite phase parameter is needed in the general theorem.
residual_risks: This checks the sharp bound uniformly over the specified offset family, not a formula for arbitrary shifts when compatibility fails, nor a nonreal-shift theorem.
